tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
- The recorded session performed: navigate to a WordPress search results page (/ ?s=...), identify stable selectors (form[role='search'] input[name='s'], form[role='search'] input[type='submit'], #content .entry-title a), type a query and submit, then click a sidebar post link. The goal is to reproduce that flow deterministically.

Task Definition:
- Single purpose tool: given a search query (s) and a 1-based result index, navigate to the search results page, collect result links, click the specified result in the main content area, and verify the opened post by extracting its title.

Action Plan:
1) Navigate directly to http://localhost:8000/?s={s} to avoid fragile UI typing/submission steps (server-rendered GET). 2) Wait a short, explicit period for DOM/widgets to settle. 3) Extract the list of title links scoped to the main content (#content .entry-title a) with fallback to anchors containing '?p=' for this site. 4) Deterministically click the indexed anchor using an indexed XPath which resolves exactly one element. 5) Wait for navigation and extract the opened post title to verify success.

Variable Identification:
- s (string): maps directly to the site's GET parameter 's'—used in the navigation URL. Required.
- open_result_index (number): 1-based index of which search result anchor to click within the main content. Required.

Step Optimization and Justification:
- Replaced the UI typing+submit sequence with a direct navigation to '/?s={s}', as the site is WordPress server-rendered and supports query parameter searches; this avoids timing and flaky selector issues observed earlier. (PASS 2 optimization.)
- Added explicit wait steps to mitigate previous timing/navigation timeouts seen in earlier runs. These are minimal (3s before extraction, 2s after click) but can be adjusted by the caller if needed.
- Used a deterministic indexed XPath to click exactly one anchor: (//*[@id='content']//a[contains(@href,'?p=')])[{open_result_index}]. This addresses the 'strict mode violation: locator resolved to X elements' failure by selecting a single node. It also scopes to #content to avoid sidebar collisions.
- Included an extraction step before the click to return the list of available titles/URLs ('search_results')—this both documents the choices and helps callers confirm the intended index. This is essential for debugging and deterministic selection because multiple similar links exist (main content vs sidebar).

Selector and Stability Notes:
- Primary selection for titles: '#content .entry-title a' (high confidence). Fallback used here is anchors in #content whose href contains '?p=' because the recorded site used query-permalink style.
- The tool assumes the environment is already authenticated if needed (per instructions). No auth steps are included.

Failure Modes and Handling:
- If the indexed XPath resolves out-of-range (no such element) the click step will fail — caller should inspect 'search_results' output to choose a valid index.
- If the server returns 5xx/500 or the page fails to load, navigation will time out; caller should retry later or investigate server logs.

This design strictly follows the recorded, successful run's essential actions, replaces fragile UI interactions with direct URL navigation for reliability, and uses deterministic selectors and explicit waits to avoid the earlier timing/selector failures.
name: tool_search_posts.v4
description: Search the site at http://localhost:8000/ using the WordPress 's' query parameter, collect search result links (scoped to main content), and open a chosen result by 1-based index. The tool navigates directly to the search URL (avoids UI timing by using the 's' parameter), waits for results, extracts result list, clicks the chosen title, waits for navigation, and verifies the opened post by extracting its title.

steps.description: Navigate directly to the search results page using the 's' query parameter (server-rendered WordPress search).
Allow page DOM and any server-side or widget-rendered content to settle before extracting results (explicit short wait to avoid timing issues).
Extract the list of title links (href + text). Primary selector intent: '#content .entry-title a'. Fallback: anchors in #content whose href contains '?p=' (site uses query-permalink style).
steps.goal: Collect all candidate title anchors inside the main content (#content .entry-title a and fallback anchors with '?p=' in href) and sidebar recent-posts for diagnostics; output href and text for each

steps.description: Click the Nth (1-based) post link inside the main content area. Uses an indexed XPath to deterministically resolve a single anchor (scoped to #content and matching '?p=' permalink pattern).
Wait for navigation to the post page to start and initial content to load.
Confirm navigation succeeded and capture the opened post's title and URL for the caller.
steps.goal: Verify the opened page by extracting the main article title (e.g. h1.entry-title or first h1) and the page URL

input_schema.name: s
input_schema.description: Search query string – maps directly to the URL query parameter 's' (e.g. 'Microsoft Planner tips'). The value will be URL-encoded and appended to '/?s={s}'.

input_schema.name: open_result_index
input_schema.description: 1-based index of the post title link to click within the main content results (selector used: #content anchors with '?p=' href fallback). The tool clicks that link deterministically; if the index is out of range the step will fail.
